151748728.title: File:An Ancient Seal Carcass in Taylor Valley.jpg

ImageDescription.value:
Another view of a seal carcass found in Taylor Valley, one of the Antarctic Dry Valleys. Animals that die in the Dry Valleys are mummified. They don't break down and rot away like they do in more temperate climates. But how and why do they get in there? No one knows yet - seals wander in and get lost and perish. 
This seal could be years old or centuries old. It is breaking down due to erosion.

151594817.title: File:Ancient Dead Seal In Taylor Valley, Antarctica.jpg

ImageDescription.value:
This seal was found in Taylor Valley one of the Antarctic Dry Valleys. Animals that die in the Dry Valleys are mummified. They don't break down and rot away like they do in more temperate climates. No one knows why the seals go into the dry valleys, but they regularly wander in, get lost, and perish. 
This particular seal carcass could be a few years old, a few decades old, or even centuries old.

The field camp called F6 sits on the shore of Lake Fryxell in Taylor Valley, McMcMurdo Dry Valleys. The camp is primarily used by the McMurdo Long Term Ecological Research program for studies on the ephemeral streams that flow through the area in the brief summer and their connection to the rest of the polar desert ecosystem.
